blogs.title: xLSTM in Plain English: Why LSTMs Are Making a Comeback
blogs.description: A high-level tour of xLSTM and why it matters now. Covers the historical rise of LSTMs, how Transformers took the lead, and what the paper changes: exponential gates, new memory designs, and residual xLSTM blocks that scale to LLM sizes.

blogs.title: Exponential Gating, Explained: How xLSTM Learns to Revise Its Memory
blogs.description: An intuitive deep-dive into the new exponential input/forget gates and the stabilizer/normalizer states. Shows how xLSTM overcomes the classic LSTM limitation of non-revisable storage decisions, with examples like parity and nearest-neighbor tasks.

blogs.title: From Scalars to Matrices: The mLSTM Memory That Remembers More
blogs.description: Breaks down the matrix memory in mLSTM and the covariance update rule. Compares it to attention-style associative recall and fast weights, and explains why it boosts capacity for rare tokens and long-range associations—while remaining parallelizable.

blogs.title: sLSTM vs mLSTM: When to Mix Memory and When to Parallelize
blogs.description: Clarifies the two xLSTM variants. sLSTM offers memory mixing and strong state tracking; mLSTM offers matrix memory and full parallelism. Explains heads, cells, and how xLSTM[ratio] stacks the two to balance capacity, speed, and expressivity.

blogs.title: Inside the xLSTM Block: Residual Backbones That Scale Like LLMs
blogs.description: Walks through xLSTM block design: pre-/post-up-projection choices, LayerNorm placement, and why non-linear summarization in higher-dimensional spaces helps (Cover’s Theorem). Shows how stacking blocks yields full xLSTM architectures.

blogs.title: Performance Report: xLSTM vs Transformers, SSMs, and RWKV
blogs.description: Summarizes the experiments: 15B and 300B-token training, validation perplexity, PALOMA across 571 domains, long-context extrapolation to 16k, and associative recall. Highlights xLSTM’s favorable scaling laws and strong downstream task results.

blogs.title: Efficiency at Scale: Linear Compute, Constant Memory, and Throughput
blogs.description: Explains why xLSTM’s recurrent design yields linear-time generation and constant memory w.r.t. context, enabling larger batch sizes and higher throughput than attention. Discusses parallel mLSTM, optimized sLSTM CUDA, and practical latency trade-offs.

blogs.title: Limitations and What’s Next: Faster Kernels, Longer Contexts, Better Inits
blogs.description: An honest look at current bottlenecks—sLSTM non-parallelism, mLSTM’s d×d cost, gate initialization sensitivity, and kernel maturity. Outlines clear paths to improvement and where xLSTM could reshape RL, time series, and physical modeling.
